en: Oda
A short test campaign: a cellar, a road and a goblin camp. It exercises every system a campaign can use.
Millbrook (test campaign)
Good bread. Good beds. I could get used to this.
Something was feeding them. Those are goblin boots.
Just the big one. The rest must be out on the road.
Something with teeth, by the look of those sacks.
You step back out into the street, pack heavier than before.
Something moves in the clearing ahead.
Millbrook is a village of one street, one well, and one mill that has stopped turning.
The goblin boss drops the coat, and Oda's grain money spills out of the lining.
It will not budge. You find the coal chute instead and slither down into the dark.
A pot clatters under your boot. Every head turns.
You are among the carts before anyone looks up.
A crowd of crows lifts off a dead ewe, complaining. Nothing else stirs.
It gives with a crack, and the smell of wet grain rolls out.
The cellar door is swollen shut with damp.
You run, and the goblins' laughter follows you down the road.
You scramble back up into daylight. Oda looks at you, then at the door, and says nothing.
You catch your breath on the cellar steps and follow the tracks out onto the road.
You land badly among the sacks. Nothing broken, but everything in there heard you.
The miller is waiting on the bridge, wringing a floury cap in both hands.
The miles pass without trouble.
Creep closer along the ditch.
Show me the door.
I'll need supplies first.
Walk straight in.
What's in the cellar?
Rain sets in as you crest the hill, and the old mill yard is below you.
Eyes in the lamplight. Two pairs, low down.
Somebody lost a purse down here, and the rats found it first.
The last rat goes still. Behind the grain bins, a nest of chewed sacking.
You rest in the lee of a wall before going down.
The road north runs between hedges gone wild.
The road is quiet again.
The sun comes out as you crest the hill, and the old mill yard is below you.
This is the end of the test campaign.
Goblins have made a camp of the ruined mill: a cauldron, a stolen cart, and a big one in a stolen coat.
Oda leads you round to a low door under the millrace.
The big one grins and draws a scimitar.
You walk back into Millbrook as the mill wheel creaks and turns again.
Thank the stars. Something is in my cellar, and the grain is going missing by the sack.
Hesk's store is across the street. Tell her I sent you.
Rats. Big ones. And tracks out the back that no rat made.
You'll eat with us tonight. And take this - it's not much.
A few coins in a bandit's purse.
The mill's stolen takings, and a potion wrapped in a rag.
Two figures step into the road with drawn blades.
Crows lift off the verge, complaining.
A wolf slinks out of the hedge.
A gnawed purse, still heavy with coin.
A bundle of old torches, damp but usable.
Rats pour out from behind the grain bins.
The goblin boss kicks over the cauldron and comes for you.
